attribution.note: Zitron states the prediction in his own voice and endorses it.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the firm prediction and its restriction to roles management believes automatable. The wording supplies no deadline or universal prevalence threshold.

contract.note: The plain reading reasonably treats completed substitutions as evidence of willingness, with creative occupations as examples. It does not require every company or occupation to experience replacement.

evidence.note: Dated reporting documents the August 29, 2023 dismissal of Gizmodo's Spanish editorial staff and replacement of their work with automated translations, citing an identified former writer.

The February 28, 2024 company disclosure confirms completed contractor reductions and links them to AI doing translation and content work. The causal wording is qualified; this is employer testimony, not an independent finding or evidence of full-time employee layoffs.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents completed AI substitutions at two companies after the statement, including editorial work. Duolingo's disclosure establishes the final required case on February 28, 2024, satisfying the early-resolution rule. Its contractor distinction limits the finding but does not defeat a prediction about paid roles. The evidence establishes neither economy-wide prevalence nor replacement in every named occupation.
